conventions.convention: N ≥ 1 and k ≥ 0; V = C^k and W = C^N carry standard Hermitian forms conjugate-linear in the first variable. The adjoint is conjugate transpose and [A,B] = AB − BA.

The moment maps are μC = [B1,B2] + IJ and μR = [B1,B1†] + [B2,B2†] + II† − J†J. Stability is generation of V by words applied to I(W); costability excludes nonzero common invariant subspaces contained in ker J; regularity requires both.
Gauge transformations act as (gB1g⁻¹,gB2g⁻¹,gI,Jg⁻¹). Orbit spaces carry quotient topology. Positive FI uses stable complex data, whereas zero real FI corresponds to regular complex data.
The torus acts by (t1B1,t2B2,Ih⁻¹,t1t2hJ), with h = diag(eα⁻¹). The framing character is Σeα⁻¹ and its dual is Σeα; generated word columns acquire characters eα t1^a t2^b.

Absolute GAGA is proved on P² and P³. Its family comparison requires the stated finite locally free direct images and algebraic and analytic fiber-base-change isomorphisms; arbitrary holomorphic families over nonproper algebraic bases are not asserted to algebraize.

L∞ is z0 = 0. A monad occupies cochain degrees −1, 0, 1 and is exact at its end terms; injectivity of its first sheaf map need not mean injectivity on every fiber. The framed-sheaf Hilbert polynomial is N binomial(m+2,2) − k.
First-order deformations use Spec C[ε]/(ε²), include a specified special-fiber identification, and are quotiented by isomorphisms inducing the identity on that identification and on W.
The rank-one ASD comparison uses the round S⁴ with boundary orientation, identifies ir ∈ u(1) with r ∈ R, defines ASD by f = −*f, and defines charge as −(8π²)⁻¹∫f∧f. Its connection space is unframed.

load_bearing.statement: Fix N ≥ 1 and k ≥ 0. Framed ADHM data consist of B1,B2 ∈ End(V), I:W→V and J:V→W, with the specified moment maps, word-span stability, invariant-kernel costability, gauge action and dual-framing torus action.

For X = Pⁿ_C, n ∈ {2,3}, analytification is an exact tensor-compatible equivalence of coherent algebraic and analytic modules and preserves cohomology and global Ext in every nonnegative degree. Restriction to the fixed hyperplane commutes with analytification. The stated family comparison is an isomorphism under its explicit local-freeness and fiber-base-change hypotheses.

Assume AC. The stable complex ADHM locus has a free proper GL(V) action; its quotient is a Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold of dimension 2kN with tangent ker d1/im d0. It is also a separated smooth finite-type complex algebraic variety with a finite invariant affine word-frame atlas and geometric quotient map. Fixed quotient points have the stated unique character-valued torus lift.

Assume AC. For every ζ > 0, each stable complex ADHM orbit meets μR = ζIV in exactly one unitary orbit, inducing a compact-torus-equivariant diffeomorphism of the stated quotients. At ζ = 0, stable real-level data are costable, and each regular complex orbit meets the zero real level in exactly one unitary orbit. For k = 0 all spaces are points.

Assume AC. A torsion-free coherent sheaf on P² with the specified rank, framing and Hilbert polynomial is locally free near L∞, has the stated H⁰ and H² vanishings and H¹ dimensions, and is the middle cohomology of the displayed Beilinson monad. The relative construction holds under the explicitly stated flatness, cohomology-bundle and closed-fiber base-change hypotheses.

Assume AC. Stable complex ADHM data give the displayed framed P² monad with torsion-free middle cohomology of rank N and Hilbert polynomial N binomial(m+2,2) − k; every such framed sheaf arises uniquely modulo GL(V). The constructions are inverse for families in the stated cohomology/base-change range, which includes every specified first-order deformation. Local freeness is equivalent to costability.

concerns.concern: The sources.references title attributes arXiv:0903.3190 to 'F. Henni'. The linked paper's title page names Amar Abdelmoubine Henni: [primary source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0903.3190). This is an incorrect author initial in the source metadata.

Two sources.references titles misidentify authors: 'F. Henni' should identify Amar Abdelmoubine Henni, and 'Andrew J. Donaldson' should identify Simon Donaldson. These are directly checkable on the [Henni title page](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0903.3190) and [Donaldson arXiv record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.08639).

Proof step 5.1 says that a change by d0(ξ) 'induces the corresponding chain homotopy fixing the relative framing and special-fiber identification'. The gauge transformation 1+εξ supplies a chain isomorphism between the deformed monads, reducing to the identity. It is not a chain homotopy in the usual degree −1 sense: the relevant global maps from O to O(−1), and from O(1) to O, vanish. The tangent quotient argument uses the chain isomorphism and remains available.

seams_checked.note: GAGA A3 uses coherence, coherent-module closure and local finite partial resolutions; it explicitly avoids importing a global analytic free resolution.
GAGA A1 uses the faithfully flat finite-type local-ring comparison, preserving nilpotents, and explicitly distinguishes it from relative direct-image comparison.
The dimension-stabilization argument uses finite-dimensional coherent cohomology only on Pʳ with 0 ≤ r ≤ 3, within the supplier's range.
GAGA A5 imports only H⁰(O) = C and positive-degree scalar vanishing in dimensions zero through three; positive-twist coherent vanishing and generation are derived locally.

The fixed-point lemma faithfully uses word-frame geometry, the unique torus lift and tangent quotient. The counting theorem's A1 retains the monad correspondence's stated family/base-change range and dual-framing convention.
The checked consumers distinguish absolute P³ GAGA from conditional relative comparison, use the zero-FI quotient only for regular data, and preserve costability as the locally-free P² locus.
The zero-charge example uses the vacuous k = 0 conditions. The positive-FI boundary example uses the exact monad signs and distinguishes stable torsion-free data from the zero-FI regular locus.
The rank criterion preserves the raw moments and stability/costability definitions. The normal-form theorem invokes the zero-level quotient after establishing regularity and both zero moments.
The zero-charge and one-instanton examples reproduce the raw gauge, moment-map and regularity conventions without strengthening the cited definitions.
